T01.clarifyQuestion: What job fails today: finding a charge, understanding status, or spotting fraud?
T01.assumptionDetail: the dominant job is finding and understanding a specific charge, not building a full insights product yet
T01.customerTryingTo: find a specific charge and understand what it means so they can decide what to do next
T01.todayTheyHaveTo: scan a chronological ledger that is accurate but hard to search, interpret, or act on
T01.focusPart: successful find-and-understand for the largest validated pain
T01.focusBecause: if they still can't identify a charge confidently, every richer insight feature sits on a broken foundation
T01.optionA: improve search, filters, and enriched transaction detail
T01.optionAHelpsWhen: customers know roughly what they're looking for but can't locate or interpret it quickly
T01.optionB: build a comprehensive insights and recurring-bills hub
T01.choiceWhy: it starts where customers are today and unlocks the next step with less scope than a full insights product
T01.customerWalkthrough: search or filter to the charge, see a recognizable merchant and clear status, then take a recovery or follow-up action if needed
T01.tradeoff: I'm deferring a broad insights hub until find-and-understand is reliable for the top pain
T01.successIf: identify the right transaction successfully and need fewer unresolved lookup contacts
T01.earlySign: higher successful search/filter completion and fewer "where's this charge" contacts
T01.concernIf: we mislabel merchant or posting state, or expose private transaction data
T01.verifyCompare: customers with the enriched history vs today's ledger on successful identification rate and unresolved lookup contacts
T01.changeMindIf: research shows the dominant pain is planning cash flow, not finding charges — then insights may deserve to come first

T02.clarifyQuestion: Do they mean bank submission, payment-network completion, or biller credit?
T02.assumptionDetail: they're asking whether the bank successfully submitted the payment, not whether the utility has credited them yet
T02.customerTryingTo: confirm that a bill payment went through so they can stop worrying or avoid paying twice
T02.todayTheyHaveTo: infer status from unclear wording that may overstate what the bank can actually prove
T02.focusBecause: ambiguous "paid" language creates repeat checks, support contacts, and duplicate payment risk
T02.optionA: clarify bank-side status, reference, and timestamp on payment detail
T02.optionAHelpsWhen: the uncertainty is about what the bank did, and we already have authoritative submission data
T02.choiceWhy: a truthful receipt solves the immediate uncertainty with fewer external dependencies than biller confirmation
T02.customerWalkthrough: open the payment, see biller, amount, bank status, date, and reference, and understand what is and isn't confirmed
T02.tradeoff: I'm not claiming biller credit yet — that stays out of scope until the integration is feasible and valuable
T02.successIf: identify payment status correctly and stop unresolved "did it go through" inquiries
T02.earlySign: fewer repeat status checks on the same payment within a short window
T02.concernIf: we imply the bill is paid at the utility when we only know bank submission
T02.verifyCompare: customers on the clearer receipt vs today on successful status identification and duplicate repayment incidents
T02.changeMindIf: most anxiety is specifically about biller credit and a reliable confirmation path is available

T03.clarifyQuestion: What observable behaviours define primary use for this customer segment?
T03.assumptionDetail: primary means recurring inbound income plus meaningful outgoing use, not just an open account
T03.customerTryingTo: decide whether Questbank can become their everyday bank for income and bills
T03.todayTheyHaveTo: open or fund an account without a clear path from first deposit to real routines like payroll and billers
T03.focusBecause: customers can "try" banking without moving income and bills — and that never becomes primary use
T03.optionA: a progressive switching journey: first deposit, card use, payroll, then billers
T03.optionAHelpsWhen: the barrier is sequencing and trust in the next routine, not just a missing promo
T03.optionB: promotional rewards for balances and transactions
T03.choiceWhy: durable routine adoption and trust beat incentives that don't create reliable utility
T03.customerWalkthrough: fund once, complete one meaningful use, then get a clear next step toward payroll or a key biller
T03.tradeoff: rewards can complement later, but I'm not leading with paid adoption that can reverse when the promo ends
T03.successIf: show recurring inbound income and meaningful outgoing use in a month
T03.earlySign: first funded account progressing to a second distinct everyday use within a defined window
T03.concernIf: missed bill or payroll harm, financial complaints, or unsustainable reward economics
T03.verifyCompare: switcher cohorts on the guided path vs control on primary-usage threshold and complaint rates
T03.changeMindIf: the main drop-off is purely price-sensitive and utility is already proven — then incentives may be the lever

T04.clarifyQuestion: For which payment type, and what milestone can the bank prove?
T04.assumptionDetail: the pain is uncertainty about status, not necessarily that the rail itself is too slow
T04.customerTryingTo: know where their transfer is and what they should do next
T04.todayTheyHaveTo: interpret a green success screen that can overstate what actually completed
T04.focusPart: authoritative stage, reference, timing, and next action
T04.focusBecause: false completion language drives duplicate attempts and unresolved contacts
T04.optionA: show authoritative stage, reference, timing, and next action
T04.optionAHelpsWhen: customers need visibility into a real pending state the bank can prove
T04.choiceWhy: truthful status and receipt come before harder recipient-side integrations
T04.customerWalkthrough: initiate a transfer, see accepted vs processing vs completed with a reference, and know whether to wait or escalate
T04.tradeoff: I'm not solving recipient confirmation or rail latency in v1 — only truthful bank-side state
T04.successIf: correctly understand the outcome and contact us less about unresolved pending transfers
T04.earlySign: fewer "is it stuck" contacts shortly after initiation
T04.concernIf: we label something completed that isn't, prompting duplicate payments
T04.verifyCompare: status UX cohort vs today on outcome comprehension and duplicate payment attempts
T04.changeMindIf: instrumentation shows actual rail latency is the harm, and a faster rail change is feasible

T05.clarifyQuestion: Is the balance wrong or is its definition unclear?
T05.assumptionDetail: the data is usually right, but posted, available, pending, and held amounts are conflated
T05.customerTryingTo: know how much they can safely spend or transfer right now
T05.todayTheyHaveTo: guess which number is spendable when labels and components aren't clear
T05.focusPart: authoritative balance breakdown with plain labels
T05.focusBecause: if spendable amount isn't trusted, every money-movement decision feels risky
T05.optionA: balance breakdown with labels and contextual explanations
T05.optionAHelpsWhen: confusion is definitional rather than a core banking data bug
T05.choiceWhy: clarify authoritative values first; projections only help after core trust exists
T05.customerWalkthrough: open balance, see available vs posted vs holds, tap for why a hold exists, then decide to spend or wait
T05.tradeoff: I'm postponing predictive cash-flow until customers trust the live numbers
T05.successIf: correctly understand spendable balance and need fewer unresolved balance inquiries
T05.earlySign: more expand/explain interactions on holds paired with fewer balance-dispute contacts
T05.concernIf: we show a wrong spendable amount or promise a hold release we can't guarantee
T05.verifyCompare: breakdown UX vs today on balance comprehension and unresolved balance inquiries
T05.changeMindIf: the root issue is incorrect core balances, not presentation — then fix data before UX polish

T06.clarifyQuestion: Which financial decision is the customer currently struggling to make?
T06.assumptionDetail: the near-term decision is recognizing recurring obligations, not full AI coaching
T06.customerTryingTo: spot upcoming or recurring obligations so they aren't surprised
T06.todayTheyHaveTo: look at pretty charts that don't clearly improve a specific decision
T06.focusPart: explainable, high-confidence recurring-charge and upcoming-obligation context
T06.focusBecause: charts without a decision and next action don't create customer value
T06.optionAHelpsWhen: customers need one verifiable insight they can act on this week
T06.optionB: sophisticated AI financial coaching across all accounts
T06.choiceWhy: start with insights customers can verify and act on before broad advisory scope
T06.customerWalkthrough: see a high-confidence recurring item, confirm or correct it, and take a clear next step
T06.tradeoff: I'm deferring AI coaching until data quality, consent, and harm controls are proven
T06.successIf: confirm a useful action or better identify an upcoming obligation
T06.earlySign: customers confirming or correcting a recurring insight, then acting on it
T06.concernIf: wrong categorization, invasive personalization, or dangerous advice
T06.verifyCompare: insight cohort vs control on confirmed useful actions and categorization error rate
T06.changeMindIf: customers already understand obligations and the gap is advice quality with safe data

T07.clarifyQuestion: Are missed payments caused by forgetting, insufficient funds, or payment processing failure?
T07.assumptionDetail: the dominant cause is forgetting known upcoming payments, not a rail failure
T07.customerTryingTo: see what's coming due and whether they have enough available funds
T07.todayTheyHaveTo: piece together bills and balance without a trustworthy upcoming view
T07.focusPart: known upcoming-payment reminders with available-funds context
T07.focusBecause: a reminder can't fix a rail failure or a true liquidity gap — but it can prevent forgetfulness
T07.optionA: known upcoming-payment reminders and available-funds context
T07.optionAHelpsWhen: bills are known or customer-confirmed and the miss is attention, not processing
T07.optionB: automatic payment and cash sweeping on behalf of the customer
T07.choiceWhy: match the intervention to the root cause and require authorization before automation
T07.customerWalkthrough: see upcoming known bills beside available balance, get a timely reminder, and choose to fund or pay
T07.tradeoff: I'm not auto-paying or sweeping cash without explicit authorization
T07.successIf: reduce avoidable missed payments among eligible customers
T07.earlySign: reminder open/action rate before due date among customers with known bills
T07.concernIf: false due dates, failed debits, or alert fatigue
T07.verifyCompare: reminder cohort vs control on avoidable missed payments and alert opt-outs
T07.changeMindIf: root cause is insufficient funds or rail failure — then reminders alone won't be the first move

T08.clarifyQuestion: Which funding step fails: link, instruction, settlement, or motivation?
T08.assumptionDetail: the largest drop-off is operational or comprehension failure in first funding, not missing cash bonuses
T08.customerTryingTo: fund the new account and get to a first useful banking action
T08.todayTheyHaveTo: open an account that never becomes funded or used because the next step is unclear or failing
T08.focusPart: first funding guidance and error recovery
T08.focusBecause: an opened account that never funds delivers no value and never becomes primary banking
T08.optionA: improve first funding guidance and error recovery
T08.optionAHelpsWhen: instrumentation shows drop-off at a concrete funding step with fixable friction
T08.optionB: offer cash bonuses for initial deposits
T08.choiceWhy: fix proven operational issues before paying people to work around them
T08.customerWalkthrough: hit a clear next funding step, recover from a common error, and complete first successful deposit
T08.tradeoff: I'm not leading with bonuses that can mask broken funding UX
T08.successIf: complete first successful funding within 30 days
T08.earlySign: higher completion at the previously failing funding step
T08.concernIf: failed or returned deposits, fraud, or misleading availability claims
T08.verifyCompare: guided funding cohort vs control on 30-day first-funding rate and failed deposit rate
T08.changeMindIf: funnel is smooth and the gap is purely motivation — then a carefully scoped incentive may be justified

T09.clarifyQuestion: Which step is delayed: debit, settlement, brokerage posting, or purchasing power?
T09.assumptionDetail: bank-side "transferred" is not the same as available-to-trade
T09.customerTryingTo: move money between banking and investing and know when they can actually use it
T09.todayTheyHaveTo: interpret one status that conflates bank and brokerage milestones
T09.focusPart: a cross-product timeline with separate bank and investment milestones
T09.focusBecause: false available-to-trade claims create mismatched expectations and support load
T09.optionA: cross-product timeline with separate bank and investment milestones
T09.optionAHelpsWhen: the money is moving correctly but customers can't tell which milestone they're waiting on
T09.choiceWhy: truthful visibility first; investigate real delay separately from status confusion
T09.customerWalkthrough: start a transfer, see bank debit vs brokerage receipt vs available-to-trade as distinct steps
T09.tradeoff: I'm not promising instant purchasing power across products in v1
T09.successIf: correctly understand status and raise fewer ambiguous funding inquiries
T09.earlySign: fewer "where is my money / can I trade" contacts during in-flight transfers
T09.concernIf: false available-to-trade claims or mismatched balances across products
T09.verifyCompare: timeline UX vs today on status comprehension and ambiguous funding contacts
T09.changeMindIf: the real harm is settlement delay we can safely shorten — then productize that after visibility

T10.clarifyQuestion: Which rails, lifecycle milestones, and customer-visible claims are in scope?
T10.assumptionDetail: we're designing status projection for delayed or failed payment events, not inventing completion
T10.customerTryingTo: trust what the app says when processing is delayed or an event fails
T10.todayTheyHaveTo: live with status that can regress, duplicate, or claim completion too early
T10.focusPart: reliable event-driven status projection with authoritative lookup
T10.focusBecause: a delay is not failure, and fabricated completion is worse than an honest unknown
T10.optionA: payment service publishes versioned events to a normalized status projection
T10.optionAHelpsWhen: we need scalable, deduped, ordered updates without hammering upstreams
T10.optionB: poll every upstream system on every screen view
T10.choiceWhy: event-driven projection plus authoritative lookup when needed beats fragile per-view polling
T10.customerWalkthrough: see only supported states, including unknown, with a clear next action and no false completion
T10.tradeoff: I'm accepting more engineering rigor up front instead of a simpler poll-everything UI shortcut
T10.successIf: see timely correct status and understand the outcome
T10.earlySign: lower rate of state regressions and false completion incidents in staging chaos tests
T10.concernIf: state regression, false completion, or missing reversal
T10.verifyCompare: happy-path, duplicate, delayed, and out-of-order event cases against authoritative financial state
T10.changeMindIf: event infrastructure can't meet correctness bars — then narrow claims and rely on authoritative lookup more

T11.clarifyQuestion: Do family members need to view information or transact on each other's behalf?
T11.assumptionDetail: the near-term need is helping someone understand a payment, not full household delegation
T11.customerTryingTo: help a family member with a banking task without oversharing
T11.todayTheyHaveTo: use screenshots or workarounds that are bad for privacy and unclear for permissions
T11.focusPart: scoped, redacted sharing or joint views for the least privileged use case
T11.focusBecause: household coordination is real, but permissions and privacy vary by relationship
T11.optionA: scoped, redacted transaction sharing or joint-account views
T11.optionAHelpsWhen: assistance means explaining one payment, not granting spend authority
T11.choiceWhy: start with least privilege; expand only with proper authorization, audit, and revocation
T11.customerWalkthrough: preview a redacted receipt, share limited fields, and complete the help task without full account access
T11.tradeoff: I'm not shipping full delegated multi-user banking until identity, permissions, and legal review are ready
T11.successIf: complete the household task with minimum information exposure
T11.earlySign: successful shares that stay within scoped fields and don't escalate to password sharing
T11.concernIf: unauthorized data access or accidental oversharing
T11.verifyCompare: scoped-share cohort vs baseline on task success and unauthorized-access incidents
T11.changeMindIf: research shows the dominant job truly requires delegated transacting with clear legal cover

T12.clarifyQuestion: What exactly is required, effective when, and which customer flows are affected?
T12.assumptionDetail: the change can invalidate an "instant" promise and must be enforced in backend state, not only copy
T12.customerTryingTo: move money with clear expectations when rules change how fast transfers can complete
T12.todayTheyHaveTo: rely on launch messaging that may no longer be legally accurate for in-scope flows
T12.focusPart: narrow scope and enforce compliant state with transparent UX
T12.focusBecause: copy-only fixes leave illegal or non-compliant processing risk in the system
T12.optionA: narrow scope and implement enforced compliant state with transparent UX
T12.optionAHelpsWhen: legal scope is clear and we can prove holds/release rules in orchestration
T12.optionB: keep schedule and only update customer-facing copy
T12.choiceWhy: align Legal, Risk, engineering, and leadership — delay or limit launch if compliance can't be proven
T12.customerWalkthrough: hit an affected flow, see a truthful held/delayed state, and understand timing without an illegal instant promise
T12.tradeoff: I may delay or limit launch rather than preserve marketing that isn't compliant
T12.successIf: process in-scope flows successfully under the new rules
T12.earlySign: compliant hold/release behavior in test suites for every affected rail before launch
T12.concernIf: early release, audit gaps, or illegal transactions
T12.verifyCompare: affected flows pre/post against legal requirements, audit completeness, and customer comprehension of timing
T12.changeMindIf: legal confirms the flow is out of scope — then we can restore the faster path for that segment only
